finding_dispositions.note: scope.md 3.5, new 4.7, 7.4 and 10 item 3 and the Bellarmine binding (loci and context) now report Bellarmine's conclusion at line 61 ('not unlikely') and also his Preface I verdict at line 47 ('acceptable' but Davidic view 'more probable'), which the finding did not cite. They set this beside Augustine's Enarr. 89.2 as a real disagreement, list Athanasius, Hilary, Jerome's letter to Cyprian, De civ. Dei XVII.14 and Theodoret's preface as leads, and state what the studies may say with no date for Moses or for an occasion.

interpretations.md adds an unsung-context rule. Reading 3 is retitled 'The Church's exodus toward the judgment', and its question, controlling claim, Communion and Gradual rows, literal and allegorical senses, limits and the section 4.2 and 4.6 notes now rest on quando facies ... iudicium, in die malo, voluit rationem ponere, In exitu Israel, a saeculo ... tu es and immortalitatis alimoniam. Ps 118:84a and Ps 89:3-12 are labelled unsung context. Augustine's Enarr. 118.84 is split into his comment on the unsung 84a (reported only as his) and on the sung 84b (the Church remains on earth until the judgment). scope.md 1.2 and 3.10 match.

summary: Repaired both research findings. RES-001: I re-read Bellarmine's two prefaces and now record his own judgment on Ps 89 (Preface II, line 61: Mosaic authorship of the titled psalms 'not unlikely'; Preface I, lines 45-47: 'acceptable', with the Davidic view 'more probable') against Augustine's Enarr. 89.2, as a real disagreement with no date. RES-002: reading 3 is re-anchored in the sung words, every use of Ps 118:84a and Ps 89:3-12 is labelled unsung context, and the record states how Augustine's and Bellarmine's comments bear on the sung v. 84b. Advisories cleared while in these files: Cassiodorus and Theodoret were read on the psalms, Alphonsus's Sermon L was found and read, the fi-ligature words were transcribed as printed, and the Aquinas Ps 118:157 join was corrected.
